frontiers.hint: Up through the vent: the canopy floor — a landscape grown on top of the glasshouse roof, where the plants that left live now. The escaped collection, doing well. Verdigris on abyss, moonlit from much closer up.
Heat. Something on the other side is burning, or cooking, or alive and enormous. A furnace room, a kitchen at the end of the world, the inside of a sleeping animal.
A door built to open in a direction you do not have. Behind it: a room with inconsistent geometry, or a folding place, or the same hall again but wrong.
Should open only from the far side. This is the natural EXIT of a future region, discovered from behind. Build the region first, then link back through here.
Scale. Behind it: somewhere built for something small, drawn at a scale that makes the player feel enormous. A lit room, occupied, tidy.
Should never actually open. A late-game payoff at most. If a future run wants to use it, the reward is a corridor identical to this one with a single detail changed.
The upper deck. Gated behind the console flag, so it must stay reachable ONLY after the console fires. Behind it: the flight deck, or a nursery, or the place the crew went.
Deeper into the craft, which is bigger inside than out. Behind it: a garden under grow-lights, a corridor that loops, or the hall of doors again seen from a wrong angle.
The clearing. Round, mown, deliberate — someone maintains it. Something is kept at the centre of it. This is the heart of the wood region: build it as a hub with its own doors deeper in.
